text.p: Shareholders of Russian utility AO Samaraenergo approved the issue of a third 100 billion rouble tranche of convertible seven-year bonds at their annual general meeting on Friday, a company spokesman told Reuters on Monday.

Takhir Khalmeyev, head of Samaraenergo's securities department, said shareholders also approved 20.1 million new ordinary shares, each with a face value of 1,000 roubles, to be used to convert the bonds.
"These shares will only be used to convert the bonds. A share issue is not planned in the near future at all," he said.
Khalmeyev said the company had laid off 400 workers already this year and had prepared a plan to cut costs in the second half of the year.
Shareholders also chose AO Auditenergo to audit the company's accounts in 1997.
Samaraenergo's main shareholder is national utility UES, which holds 56 percent of shares in the company. Foreign shareholders hold 22 percent of shares.
Samaraenergo is a deficit producer and buys 25 percent of its electricity on the Federal Wholesale Market (FOREM).
